title: Observability Sidecar Decommission & Migration Playbook
author: Ayesha Patel
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines the safe, repeatable process for migrating away from per-service observability sidecars and either consolidating telemetry into a lightweight instrumentation shim or adopting platform-managed collectors. The objective is to reduce operational cost, simplify upgrade paths, and remove sidecar-induced availability and resource noise while preserving (and improving) SLI continuity and traceability.

When to apply this playbook:
- Sidecar is causing high memory/CPU variance across nodes.
- Sidecar lifecycle is blocking service upgrades (hot-restart/preemption problems).
- There are platform-managed collectors available that provide equivalent guarantees.
- Security/compliance prevents unmanaged binaries in constrained environments.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: migration of telemetry sidecars that perform metrics, traces, and logs collection for services owned by Redwood teams. Includes deployment, rollout, verification, and decommission.
- Non-goals: this playbook is not for migrating application-level policy sidecars (e.g., security proxies) or for rewriting instrumentation libraries.

Stakeholders and ownership:
- Migration Owner (per service): service team lead (engineering).
- Observability Platform: eng-platform (owners of collectors, schema contracts, retention).
- SRE & Reliability: eng-sre (SLO verification, burn-rate rules).
- Security & Compliance: security-and-compliance (sign-off on binaries and network egress).
- Release Coordination: eng-infra (change windows and CI gating).

Pre-migration checklist (all items must be green before starting):
1) Inventory: list services using sidecars, sidecar versions, config keys, and endpoints.
2) Schema compatibility: ensure Prometheus metric names, labels, and OpenTelemetry resource attributes are covered by platform collectors.
3) Contract tests: add/execute schema contract tests for metrics and trace spans.
4) Backfill plan: identify time ranges where missing telemetry would be acceptable and communicate to downstream consumers.
5) Canary target: identify canary host(s) or namespace with low customer impact.
6) Security review: binary signing, CVE scan results attached.
7) RBAC & network: platform collectors can access service endpoints and logs without exposing new risks.

Migration procedure (step-by-step):
1) Prepare a lightweight shim:
   - If sidecar was enriching spans or applying local sampling, implement a minimal shim library (language-specific) that preserves necessary attributes but forwards to the platform collector endpoint.
   - Example shim responsibilities: set service.name, deployment.region, request_id propagation, and enforce local sampling hints as tags (do not drop spans unless explicitly approved).

2) Deploy platform-managed collector in passive mode beside the service:
   - Configure collector to receive via OTLP/HTTP or gRPC; enable auto-label mappings.
   - Passive mode means collector will only receive and forward; it will not alter sampling decisions or perform aggregation that changes semantics.

3) Run dual-write canary:
   - For 72 hours, configure the service to write both to existing sidecar and to the platform collector.
   - Metrics: export a subset of high-cardinality metrics to the platform to measure parity.

4) Validate parity and correctness:
   - Compare counts, latencies, and error rates between sidecar and collector using the comparison dashboard provided by eng-platform.
   - Run span-level checksum tests for a sample of traces (span count, attributes, and parent-child relationships).

5) Gradual rollout:
   - 10% traffic -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% (minimum 2 hours between increments, extend if anomalies observed).
   - At each step, run automated checks: SLI delta < 2% for error rate, <5ms median latency delta for tracing spans that impact path timing, and <5% cardinality delta for key metrics.

6) Disable sidecar in rolling fashion:
   - Maintain canary until 24h after 100% traffic is on platform collector.
   - For each pod/node, remove sidecar container and confirm service restarts cleanly and healthchecks pass.

7) Decommission:
   - Retire sidecar configs and images from CI/CD pipelines.
   - Update runbooks and onboarding docs to reference new collector endpoints and shim libraries.
   - Remove older sidecar binaries from allowed images list in policy registries after 30 days.

Verification and SLO evidence:
- Required evidence artifacts (attach to migration ticket):
  - Parity dashboards showing metric/time-series comparisons.
  - Sample trace comparison report (trace IDs and checksum diffs).
  - Alert spike analysis (if any) during rollout window.
  - SLIs to monitor post-decommission:
    - Request success rate (SLO: 99.9% monthly).
    - Trace ingestion coverage for 99th percentile latency paths (target: no worse than pre-migration baseline + 5%).
    - Metric cardinality and label fidelity (verify <10% unexpected new labels).

Rollback plan (fast and safe):
- Fast rollback: If SLI delta beyond thresholds is observed within an increment window, pause rollout and revert traffic routing to sidecar write. Restore sidecar on pods if removed.
- Slow rollback: Reintroduce dual-write for 24h and run detailed drift analysis before reattempting a staged rollout.

Risk matrix (top risks and mitigations):
- Data loss during cutover: mitigate with dual-write and retention of sidecar-forwarded buffers for 72h.
- Sampling divergence: require sampling policy parity tests in contract test suite.
- Increased cardinality from platform collector labels: enforce label allowlist at ingestion.
- Resource regressions: run load test benchmark against the platform collector under expected peak QPS.

Configuration examples:
- OTEL collector snippet (illustrative):
  receivers:
    otlp:
      protocols:
        grpc: 
        http: 
  processors:
    batch:
  exporters:
    platform_exporter:
      endpoint: "collector.platform-redwood.internal:4317"
  service:
    pipelines:
      traces:
        receivers: [otlp]
        processors: [batch]
        exporters: [platform_exporter]

- Kubernetes rollout command examples:
  - kubectl apply -f service-with-shim.yaml --context=canary
  - kubectl rollout status deployment/my-service --namespace=canary
  - kubectl patch deployment my-service -p "{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"observability.migration/redwood":"dual-write"}}}}}"

Operational notes and housekeeping:
- Nightly job: eng-platform will run a 1am parity check and post results to the migration ticket automatically (requires permission token).
- Policy: sidecar images must remain in CI allowlist until 30 days after decommission.
- Change windows: prefer low-traffic windows (weekend overnight) for final 100% cutovers for customer-facing services.

Post-mortem and learning feedback loop:
- After every migration complete, schedule a 1-hour retro with service, eng-platform, and eng-sre. Capture: what metrics drifted, alerts fired, time to rollback, and suggested automation improvements.
- Maintain a migrations registry (eng-platform-owned) with status (planned/active/retired) and lessons learned summaries.

Appendix: artifact checklist for migration ticket:
- Inventory CSV attached
- Schema contract test results (link)
- Security scan + binary signature evidence
- Dashboard links for parity and SLI baselines
- Rollout timeline and change-window approval

If you have questions or need a migration review, contact eng-platform@redwood.internal or open a ticket with label observability-migration.
